Everything here was established empirically against live Meson endpoints on 2026-10-27/28 and verified field-by-field against the rendered explorer page.
This file exists so nobody has to repeat the reverse-engineering.

## The problem

A support ticket needs: transaction hash, from chain, to chain, amount, wallet address, explorer link. No single Meson endpoint returns all of that.

## What the documented API does and does not give you

The official docs at <https://meson.dev> describe a relayer API:

| Endpoint | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `GET relayer.meson.fi/api/v1/swap?hash=<tx>` | event hashes + `expired`; since 2026-10-28 also chains, tokens, amounts (no addresses) |
| `GET relayer.meson.fi/api/v1/swap/<swapIdOrEncoded>` | the same |
| `GET relayer.meson.fi/api/v1/list` | chains + token symbols/decimals/addresses |

When this was first written (2026-10-27) the two `swap` endpoints looked **status-only**: a map like `{BONDED, LOCKED, EXECUTED, RELEASED}` of transaction hashes plus an `expired` flag.
Re-checked 2026-10-28: they now also carry `swap: {id, encoded, from: {amount, network, token}, to: {amount, network, token}}` — chains, tokens and amounts as display strings (`"179.276362"`, network ids like `xlayer`, `bnb`).
Still missing: **wallet addresses** (initiator / recipient), failed attempts, pending flags and the request time — so it still cannot fill the details embed or derive the explorer's status.
Both resolve a swap ID, an encoded swap and a source tx hash; unknown → HTTP 404 `{"error":{"code":-1,"message":"swap-not-found"}}`.
No batching: `/swap/<id>,<id>` answers "swap-not-found".
It is a separate host from the explorer, so it is the one usable stand-in if `explorer.meson.fi` itself is down (degraded: no addresses, no exact status).

`/api/v1/list` returns 43 chains with real token symbols (it correctly reports that `usdt` on BNB displays as `BSC-USD`), but it carries **no `tokenIndex` and no `slip44`**, which are exactly the two numbers an encoded swap contains — so it cannot decode a swap, and the bot does not use it.

## What the explorer API gives you

The explorer is a Next.js app.
The swap page is *not* server-rendered with data — the HTML contains only the swap ID — so the data comes from client-side calls on the explorer's own origin.
All work unauthenticated, with no API key:

```
GET https://explorer.meson.fi/api/v1/search?q=<anything>
    -> {"result":{"swapId":"0x…"}}

GET https://explorer.meson.fi/api/v1/swap/<swapId>
    -> {"result":{ _id, encoded, events[], srFee, lpFee, initiator,
                   fromTo[from,to], created, executed, released, batchTo }}

GET https://explorer.meson.fi/api/v1/swap/<swapId>,<swapId>,…
    -> {"result":[ <same shape as /api/v1/swap/<id>, one per swap found> ]}

GET https://explorer.meson.fi/api/v1/address/<address>/swap?page=0&size=10
    -> {"result":{"list":[ <same shape as /api/v1/swap/<id>, repeated> ]}}
```

`search` is the useful discovery: one endpoint resolves **all** of these to a swap ID — swap ID, encoded swap, EVM transaction hash, and Solana signature (base58).
Verified against all four, and (2026-10-28) for destination-side release hashes too — an EVM one and the release hash of a Solana swap.
Unknown input returns `{"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"Swap not found"}}` with HTTP 400 *or* 404 (`/api/v1/swap/<id>` uses 400), so error handling must look at the body, not the status.

`/api/v1/swap/<id>,<id>,…` (comma-separated swap IDs, checked 2026-10-28) answers with an **array** of the same records as the single lookup, byte-for-byte: sorted by ID (not request order), duplicates merged, unknown IDs silently left out (all unknown → `[]`, HTTP 200).
A single ID still answers with the object (or the "not found" error), not an array.
20 IDs in one request worked (the most tested).
This is what lets the bot re-check every watched swap in one request (`getSwaps`, `src/meson.js`).
Because it is undocumented, `getSwaps` looks up on its own every ID the batch did not deliver (left out, or the batch request failed — an unknown explorer API path answers with an HTML 404 page). When those single lookups find swaps, it logs `batch lookup … while single lookups work — Meson may have changed …` and skips the batch for an hour before trying it again — that log line is the sign Meson changed this endpoint.
`/api/v1/swap?ids=…` and `/api/v1/swaps?ids=…` do **not** work — the first ignores `ids` and lists recent swaps, the second is an HTML page.

`/api/v1/address/<address>/swap` returns every swap the address took part in on *either* side (sender or recipient), newest first — this is what backs the explorer's "Swaps for Address" page.
It takes `page` (0-based) and `size`.
There is no total-count field in the response; `list.length === size` is the only signal that another page might exist, confirmed against a real address with 14 swaps across two pages of 10.
Each list entry is the exact same record shape as the single-swap endpoint, so the same decode/status logic applies unchanged — `toSwapView()` in `src/meson.js` is shared by the single, batch and address endpoints.

Limits of the address endpoint (checked against the live API and the explorer's own front-end code):

- `size` above 20 is rejected: `{"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"Size cannot exceed 20"}}`.
- There is **no status or date filter**.
  The front-end only ever adds `failed=true` or `rewardId=…`; `failed=true` returned a Done swap, so it does not filter either.
  Made-up params (`status=`, `type=`, …) are ignored.
- `/api/v1/address/<address>/export` exists but answers 401 without a login.

So "this wallet's unfinished swaps" can only be found by paging newest-first and filtering locally, which is why the bot bounds it by age and page count.

## Other public endpoints found in the explorer's code (2026-10-28)

Found by reading the explorer's own JavaScript (every chunk the public pages load), then calling each path.
GET only — the code also has write calls (`PUT /api/v1/swap/<encoded>`, `DELETE …/swap/from-contract/<encoded>`, blacklist edits) used by Meson's staff tools; never call those.

| Endpoint | Public? | What it gives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `explorer…/api/v1/swap/<encoded>` | yes | The swap record by its encoded form directly (same as by swap ID) — no `search` needed |
| `explorer…/api/v1/swap/<id>,<id>,…` | yes | Batch lookup — see above |
| `explorer…/api/v1/premium/<address>` | yes | `{token: null}` unless the wallet has Meson premium |
| `explorer…/api/v1/address/<a>/swap?failed=true` | answers, but **does not filter** for the public (one wallet: 20 of 20 returned, most without a failed step) — the "Failed" switch is an admin-only badge | — |
| `explorer…/api/v1/swap?page=&size=` | yes | Newest swaps across Meson; **ignores every filter** tried (`failed`, `from`, `to`, `token`, `category`, `status`) |
| `explorer…/api/v1/stats/*`, `…/swap/share-with/<id>`, `…/address/<a>/export` | **401** — need a Meson staff login | — |
| Pages `/pending/bonded`, `/stats/*`, `/lp`, `/relayer/<x>`, `/pool/<x>`, `/rules`, `/blacklist`, `/premium`, `/rewards` | **staff only** — the server redirects to `/` | — |
| `relayer.meson.fi/api/v1/limits` | yes | Per chain and token: `min` / `max` swap amount (e.g. USDC on Arbitrum 1.0 – 20000) — same list as `/list` plus limits |
| `relayer.meson.fi/api/v1/rules` | yes | 371 fee rules (route → minimum, fee, limit, `waiveSrFee`) plus `prices` |
| `liquidity.meson.fi/api/v1/balance?networkId=<id>&entry=pool:1` | yes | Meson's pool balance per token on one chain (`value` as a decimal string; the `_id` starts with a ms timestamp) — 0 means no liquidity there right now |
| `rpcs.meson.fi/` | yes | `{success, data: {<chainId>: [nodes]}}` — every chain's RPC nodes as Meson sees them: `healthy`, `latency`, `lastBlockNumber`, `lastBlockTimestamp`, `gasPrice` — 44 chains, keyed by the same ids as presets (`eth`, `arb`; only `b2` is not in presets). The bot's ⚠️ network notice uses it: a chain is troubled when *no* node is healthy |

Not found (404): `/api/v1/{rules,pending,lp,pool,relayer(s),rpcs,chains,list,status,health,banners,rewards,pinned-messages}` on the explorer; `/api/v1/{price,status}`, `/api/v2/swap/temp` and `abstract-initiator/<address>` (GET) on the relayer.

## The encoded swap

`result.encoded` is Meson's 32-byte packed swap.
The chains, amount and tokens live only in here — the explorer unpacks it in the browser.
Layout (big-endian, offsets inclusive-exclusive), confirmed byte-for-byte:

```
[0,1)   version
[1,6)   amount     always 6 decimals, whatever the token's own decimals are
[6,16)  salt
[16,21) fee        the LP fee, same 6-decimal units
[21,26) expireTs   unix seconds
[26,28) outChain   SLIP-44 coin type, e.g. 0x02ca = 714 = BNB
[28,29) outToken   Meson token index, scoped to outChain
[29,31) inChain
[31,32) inToken
```

Worked example — swap `0x1f399b60…`, encoded `0x01001563e611d80000000000ab47eb9b0000027100006ae0616702ca2201f502`:

| Field | Decoded | Explorer page shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| amount | 358868497 → 358.868497 | `358.868497 USDT` |
| fee | 160000 → 0.16 | `0.16` |
| inChain / inToken | `0x01f5` (501) / 2 | `Solana` / `USDT` |
| outChain / outToken | `0x02ca` (714) / 34 | `BNB Smart Chain` / `BSC-USD` |

Amounts are 6-decimal **regardless of the token**, including 8-decimal BTC: swap `0x3b1fde45…` decodes to `0.00052 WBTC → 0.000479 BTC`, matching the page.

Received amount = `amount - srFee - lpFee`. The encoded `fee` equals `lpFee`; `srFee` (service fee) is only in the JSON, so use the JSON for the total.

## Chain and token names

Checked 2026-10-28 against the public EVM chain registry (`chainid.network/chains.json`, what chainlist.org shows): all 80 of Meson's EVM mainnet chains exist there under the same chain ID; names differ only in spelling (B² Network / "B2 Mainnet", Hashkey Chain / "HSKChain") and for chain ID 999, which the registry lists as "Wanchain Testnet" but Meson uses for HyperEVM. The 9 non-EVM chains (Tron, Bitcoin, Solana, Starknet, Aptos ×2, Sui, CKB, TON) are not in that registry. `refresh-presets` used to drop chains whose bundle text contains a JavaScript-only string escape (`"B\xb2 Network"`, `"Merlin\'s Seal USDC"`), which JSON rejects; it now converts them and warns about any chain it still cannot parse.

Only one published source carries both `shortSlip44` and `tokenIndex`: the explorer's preset table, embedded in a webpack chunk (not served from any endpoint).
`scripts/refresh-presets.mjs` extracts it into `src/presets.json` (89 mainnet chains as of 2026-10-28).

**The bundle ships two preset generations.** The older one has global token indexes (`1=USDC, 2=USDT`); the current one has per-chain indexes where BNB's `34` is `BSC-USD`.
The extractor takes **later definitions win** — getting this backwards silently mislabels every token on chains that were re-indexed.

Testnets share a `shortSlip44` with their mainnet (`bnb-testnet` is also `0x02ca`), so the extractor filters testnets out before keying by slip44.

## Status derivation

The API has no status field. **The bot uses the explorer's own status function**, ported line for line as `explorerStatus` in `src/meson.js` — support wants the heading to always match what the explorer shows.
It lives in the explorer bundle (a `_next/static/chunks/*.js` chunk; search for `"FAILED","PENDING","REQUESTING"`) and is called with the swap's `events` and `expireTs`.
On 2026-10-28 the port was checked against the extracted original: identical on 1000 recent real swaps and on hand-made edge cases, and again later that day against the live bundle (chunk `6350-…`) on 2000 recent swaps — 0 differences. If the explorer changes, re-extract it and compare the same way.
The bot now notices that itself: `src/explorer-check.js` (`npm run check-explorer`) finds the function in the live bundle (from the step-rank array to its last `?"LOCKED":c}`), blanks the 1–2 character minified names, and compares a SHA-256 fingerprint with `PORTED_FINGERPRINT` — renaming variables (a redeploy) keeps it, any logic change alters it.

How it works:

1. Pick the furthest step: of events that have a hash or end in `ING` (not GASDROP) — a `pending` one counts as PENDING, a `:FAILED` one as FAILED — the highest in `FAILED < PENDING < REQUESTING < POSTED < BONDED < LOCKED < UNLOCKED < RELEASING < EXECUTED < CANCELLED < RELEASED`.
2. RELEASED → **DONE** (or **RELEASED** if there is no EXECUTED yet — the recipient has the funds, the LP has not collected).
3. CANCELLED → **CANCELLED**.
4. EXECUTED → **RELEASING...** (or **UNLOCKED** if there is an UNLOCKED). This is checked *before* the deadline, so an executed swap past `expireTs` is still Releasing; a pending or failed release also lands here, since EXECUTED outranks both.
5. RELEASING (the hashless request) → **RELEASING** if funds were taken on-chain (a hashed POSTED / BONDED / LOCKED / EXECUTED), else treated as REQUESTING.
6. Past the deadline → **EXPIRED** (`EXPIRED*` if funds were taken). With nothing on-chain the deadline counts as `expireTs − 3600`.
7. Otherwise **LOCKED** if an LP lock is outstanding, else the furthest step itself (PENDING, REQUESTING, BONDED, FAILED…).

A trailing `*` means more LOCKED than RELEASED/UNLOCKED events (an LP lock outstanding); `EXPIRED*` alone means funds were taken on-chain before it expired.
The bot keeps the `*` (support asked for it, as on the explorer), drops the `...` and title-cases the rest — "Expired*", "Releasing". In code the word and the star are separate: `status.label` ("Expired", what logic checks) and `status.star` ("*" or "", added wherever the status is displayed).

What each event means, per meson.dev (`/api/endpoints/check-swap`):

| Event | Chain | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POSTED | initial | takes the user's incoming funds (into the Meson contract) |
| BONDED | initial | an LP bonds the swap |
| LOCKED | target | LP locks funds for the swap |
| RELEASED | target | funds released to the recipient |
| EXECUTED | initial | the user's posted funds transferred to the LP |
| UNLOCKED | target | LP's lock undone (swap did not go through) |
| CANCELLED | initial | funds returned to the initiator |

So the user's funds leave their wallet at POSTED.
By those descriptions EXECUTED is the LP collecting, which should follow RELEASED — yet the explorer often lists only EXECUTED + RELEASED (no POSTED), so treat event order and presence as observed, not guaranteed.
Observed by support (2026-10): status goes Pending → Releasing → Done / Cancelled / Expired; the steps seen are BONDED (Solana only), EXECUTED, RELEASING / RELEASED and CANCELLED.
Survey of 2000 recent swaps (2026-10-28) — every event kind that occurred: RELEASED 1987, EXECUTED 1986, BONDED 151 (Solana), REQUESTING without hash 28, `RELEASED:FAILED` 10, RELEASING without hash 8, `EXECUTED:FAILED` 1, CANCELLED 1, and one swap with a `pending` EXECUTED + CANCELLED (explorer: Expired*). POSTED, LOCKED, UNLOCKED and GASDROP did not occur. 90% were plain EXECUTED + RELEASED.
Watched live (2026-10-28, 8 new swaps over 25 min): a new swap first shows **Pending** with its EXECUTED still `pending` (confirming); the RELEASED event then appears while still confirming (status stays Pending, or Releasing once EXECUTED has confirmed); then **Done** — sometimes even while EXECUTED is still confirming. Time from first sight to Done: 11 s to 10½ min, most within ~1½ min (hence `PROCESSING_MESSAGE_DELAY_SECONDS`).
In the transaction hashes list the release is one entry: releasing (the hashless request) → releasing (confirming) (RELEASED, `pending`) → released.

The bot treats only **Done**, **Released** and **Cancelled** as finished (`isFinished`): nothing is left to chase. Expired, Unlocked and Failed stay watched until the team resolves them.

**Expired** per the docs: the swap "cannot be executed on the Meson contract thereafter, and funds remain in `fromAddress`" — that is the never-POSTED case.
If it *was* POSTED, the funds are in the contract until a CANCELLED returns them.
The docs say an API-submitted swap expires after 10 minutes if blocked, but the window in `expireTs` varies (≈90 min has been observed).

Because of that, the bot's Expired text says only **"the swap was not completed in time"** — nothing about where the funds are or whether it can still go through.
Support may be able to cancel and refund it, or (if the funds are in the contract) push it to completion, so any stronger wording could be wrong.

**`REQUESTING`** is a further event the explorer returns that the docs do not list — seen alone on an expired swap, with **no `hash`** (asked for, never on-chain).
The explorer (and so the bot) shows such a swap as Requesting, or Expired once past `expireTs − 3600`; the details embed lists it as "no transaction yet".
Any event can lack a hash, so render code must not assume one.

**Failed is not a Meson status.** The docs list no `:FAILED` events; they come only from the explorer API, meaning one transaction for that step reverted.
Per the support team, a failure is never final: a failed release (e.g. low liquidity on the destination) is retried until it goes through, and a stuck swap is resolved by the team to Done (pushed through) or Cancelled (refunded).
The details embed therefore shows one entry per step — the successful hash, or else the latest attempt's, then marked "(failed)" (support's choice, 2026-10-28: a bare hash under "executed" read as if it had gone through) — and never counts or lists failed retries next to a success.
Confirmed on real swaps (2026-10-28): retries appear as repeated `RELEASED:FAILED` events next to the successful `RELEASED` (one swap had two failed attempts), and the details embed shows just the successful release.
The heading needs no special case: the explorer ranks a failed attempt lowest, so an executed swap with failed releases shows Releasing.

**`events[]` is not in time order and has no timestamps** — a cancelled swap came back as CANCELLED, EXECUTED, RELEASING (the last with no hash).
The details embed sorts steps itself (`STEP_ORDER` in `src/render.js`), and once a swap is finished (Done, Released or Cancelled) it leaves out hashless entries like that RELEASING (a request that never became a transaction).

## Per-chain explorer links

`presets.json` carries each chain's `explorer` base and `addressFormat`.
The transaction path differs by format: `/tx/` for most, `/transaction/` for Tron, CKB and TON, `/txn/` for Aptos (which also needs `?network=mainnet`), `/txblock/` for Sui.
Tron's `explorer` value already ends in `/#`.

Source-side events (posted, bonded, executed, cancelled) are on the **in** chain; `LOCKED`, `RELEASED` and `UNLOCKED` are on the **out** chain (`TARGET_CHAIN_STEPS` in `src/meson.js`). Linking them to the wrong chain is an easy mistake — until 2026-10-28 the bot linked LOCKED/UNLOCKED to the source chain (never seen in practice: neither occurred in 2000 swaps).

## Things that will break this

- The explorer API is not a documented, versioned contract.
  If `/api/v1/search` or `/api/v1/swap/<id>` changes shape, the bot breaks.
  The batch form `/api/v1/swap/<id>,<id>` is covered: if it stops working, `getSwaps` falls back to single lookups and logs it.
  The documented relayer endpoints could stand in for status, chains, tokens and amounts, but not for wallet addresses or the explorer's exact status.
- If the explorer changes its status function, our port silently disagrees with it — `src/explorer-check.js` detects that daily and logs a warning; re-port then.
- If the explorer bundle's preset layout changes, `refresh-presets.mjs` throws rather than writing a truncated table (it requires ≥40 chains).
- New chains and tokens show up as `Unknown chain (0x…)` / `token#NN` until `npm run refresh-presets` is run.
- The API never reports *when* a swap failed or was cancelled — only `released` (a real completion time) and `expireTs` (when it stops being executable).
  Don't compute a "took X" duration from `expireTs` for a non-released swap (the bot now shows only the request time anyway); it measures time to expiry, not time to failure, and the two can differ by over an hour.
